standard_prerequisites.name: The three forcing propositions chained by the proof
standard_prerequisites.statement: The COH proposition produces a cohesive set controlling the jump; the SEM proposition produces a transitive subtournament with the same control; the SADS proposition produces a homogeneous set; their statements are retained with this card at source lines 461-468, 760-767 and 1102-1109.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof applies them in sequence, each time with alpha equal to one, zero or one so that the well-foundedness requirement is met, and reads off the jump control and the homogeneity.

standard_prerequisites.name: The omega-extension result of Fiori-Carones et al
standard_prerequisites.statement: From a set P one obtains a P-computable countable coded model of WKL_0-star containing the jump of Y, hence an intermediate set P_0 below P and above the jump of Y whose model satisfies the same finite-level scheme; the citation is carried in the proof and its entry is attached with this card.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the intermediate set P_0 used by the first application, and the fact that both models satisfy the scheme at level n minus one.

standard_prerequisites.name: Complexity transfer between the model and its extension
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every Sigma^0_n formula over the extension by G_0 is Sigma^0_{n-1} over the model of P_0, so satisfaction of the scheme at level n minus one in the latter gives satisfaction of the scheme at level n in the former; the proof uses this twice.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is how the proof raises the scheme from level n minus one to level n at the first and second steps.

core_obligations: Apply the cited isomorphism result to get a P-computable model of WKL_0-star containing the jump of Y, hence a set P_0 between P and the jump of Y, and note that both models satisfy the scheme at level n minus one (source lines 1516-1517).

Define the sets induced by the colouring and apply the cohesive-set proposition with alpha equal to one to obtain an M-infinite cohesive set G_0 with the jump control and with the model of G_0 satisfying collection; note that the colouring restricted to G_0 is stable (source lines 1519-1520).

Transfer the scheme: because Sigma^0_n formulas over G_0 are Sigma^0_{n-1} over P_0 and the model of P_0 satisfies the scheme at level n minus one, the model of G_0 satisfies the scheme at level n, hence also well-foundedness of omega to the omega (source line 1521).

Apply the SEM proposition with alpha equal to one to obtain an M-infinite transitive set G_1 inside G_0 with the jump control, and transfer the scheme again by the same complexity argument (source lines 1523-1526).

Apply the SADS proposition with alpha equal to zero to obtain an M-infinite homogeneous set G inside G_1 with the jump control, and transfer the scheme a third time, which gives the three asserted properties of the counted proposition (source lines 1528-1530).

proof_roadmap.step: Get P_0 from the omega-extension result and note the scheme holds in both models.
First application, then transfer the scheme by the complexity shift.
Third application and transfer, concluding the proof.
